title: Searching for a term that contains a percent sign shows the search results page, not an error page

report.text:
Search breaks when I search for 100% stoneware

Hi,

I was looking for pieces that are fully stoneware, so I typed 100% stoneware into the search box and pressed Search. Instead of results I got an error page. Searching for just stoneware works fine.

Thanks,
Tom

reason: Checkpoint assertion failed: "the page shows a heading that reads Results for “100% stoneware”"

verdict.title: Search page shows generic error for valid stoneware query
verdict.oneLiner: Searching for “100% stoneware” shows an error page instead of search results or the expected no-results message.
verdict.rootCause: The search page failed to load a valid query and displayed a generic error message rather than the required results state.
verdict.suggestion: Investigate why the search request for “100% stoneware” reaches the generic error page, and ensure it instead renders the results heading plus product cards or the supported no-results message.

attempts.agentSummary:
The cause was a second decode of the search query in `server.js`. `url.searchParams.get('q')` already returns the decoded value, `100% stoneware`. The code then ran `decodeURIComponent` on it again, and that call throws a `URIError` on the bare `%`, which gave the 500.

I removed the extra `decodeURIComponent` call, so the route now passes the value from `searchParams` straight to `pages.search`. I haven't run the app or the flow, as instructed.

entries.label: Claude Code (opus)
entries.summary:
The search page crashed because the query was decoded twice. `url.searchParams.get('q')` already turns `100%25+stoneware` into `100% stoneware`, and then `server.js:368` ran `decodeURIComponent` on that result. A stray `%` that isn't followed by two hex digits makes it throw `URIError: URI malformed`, which the catch block turned into the 500 "Something went wrong" page.

I removed the second decode in `server.js`. I also escaped the query in the "Results for" heading with the existing `esc()` helper, because it was being inserted into the HTML raw. That doesn't change how "100% stoneware" displays. I haven't run the app or the flow, as instructed; Kane's re-run will confirm the fix.

entries.label: Claude Code (haiku)
entries.summary:
The search page crashed on any `%` in the query, so "100% stoneware" returned the 500 error page. The cause was a double decode: `url.searchParams.get('q')` already percent-decodes the value, and the extra `decodeURIComponent` then threw a `URIError` on the stray `%`, which the catch block turned into the error page.

I changed `server.js` in two places:
- **Line 368:** removed the second `decodeURIComponent` call, so the search term is passed through as already decoded.
- **Line 249:** the query is now passed through `esc()` before it goes into the "Results for" heading. This is beyond the reported crash, but the raw query was being written into HTML unescaped.

I did not run the app, Gremlin or Kane, per the session rules.
